subject: Delegation runbook: limited-time KMS access for inference-runtime vendors (audit prep)
messages:
From: Matt Kline <matt.kline@alphamed.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@alphamed.com
Date: 2025-11-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: KMS access window for vendor migration — upcoming audit

Hi David & Laura,

Quick context: AlphaMed is running a golden-path migration of historical inference logs to our analytics cluster next Tuesday; the vendor doing the job (SyncBridge) needs ephemeral read access to a subset of customer keys in your KMS to complete key-wrapping for archival. We have a compliance audit for the week after and need to capture a clean delegation runbook + evidence chain.

Can you share:
- A short runbook describing the delegation steps (who approves, how keys are scoped and revoked)
- The proposed access window (we prefer a narrow window, ideally <= 8 hours)
- Monitoring/telemetry we should expect (audit logs, alerts)

Also: procurement would like any contract amendment language for limited-scope access (we can accept a short addendum). We aim to finalize by Friday so legal can sign before the migration.

Appreciate it — Matt
Matt Kline
Security Lead, AlphaMed

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Matt Kline <matt.kline@alphamed.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-08T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: KMS access window for vendor migration — upcoming audit

Matt — thanks for the heads up.

Agree we should keep the window tight. I attached a short delegation runbook and an access matrix draft (see attachments). High-level proposal:

- Access scope: single key-chain namespace limited to archival-wrapping keys for the migration job (no read of customer plaintext).
- Access mechanism: short-lived delegated keys issued via Redwood EPHEM service (TTL = 4 hours). Keys minted with allowlist for specific vendor CIDRs and job instance IDs.
- Approval flow: Security reviewer (David Kim) + AlphaMed ops owner (Matt) must both sign the runbook. Procurement signs the addendum.
- Monitoring: KMS audit trail (key issuance + use), agent-side logging forwarded to our SIEM, and a one-hour post-runship reconciliation report.
- Revocation: automatic when TTL expires; manual revoke button in the console for emergency stop.

Next steps:
1) Laura / Ben — can you confirm we can enforce CIDR allowlist on the vendor-hosted instance?
2) Matt — confirm the preferred migration date/time window and the vendor's IPs so we can bind the delegation.
3) Procurement — I'll attach a short amendment draft for review (PDF).

Attachments: runbook_kms_delegation_v1.pdf (runbook draft), access_matrix_inference_v2.xlsx (scoped matrix).

Thanks,
David Kim
Security Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, Matt Kline <matt.kline@alphamed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-08T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: KMS access window for vendor migration — upcoming audit

Adding a couple of operational controls and evidence items so AlphaMed's audit team can close the loop quickly: 

- We will require vendor instances be NATed through the approved CIDR block and present mTLS certs that match the allowlist. That enforces source validation before EPHEM mints any delegated key.
- Logging: we'll provide a consolidated audit bundle after the migration: KMS issuance logs (JSON), SIEM alerts (summary PDF), and a reconciliation spreadsheet.

Suggested evidence deliverables for your audit:
- Runbook (signed by security + ops) — we can capture signatures via DocuSign.
- KMS issuance log slice covering the window (timestamped; CSV).
- Access matrix mapping (who approved, what key namespace, TTL).

Priyom: can you confirm CAIQ/SIG mapping to the KMS control set so the customer can map these items against their questionnaire? I can attach the mapping link once you confirm.

Ben: I'll need an SLA exception note if AlphaMed asks for an emergency 24/7 on-call number (we normally provide a pager for escalations but not continuous dedicated phone).

Laura Bennett
Director, Cloud Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Matt Kline <matt.kline@alphamed.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@alphamed.com
Date: 2025-11-09T08:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: KMS access window for vendor migration — upcoming audit

Thanks, Laura & team. This is exactly what we need. A couple of quick confirmations:

- Migration preferred window: 2025-11-18 from 02:00–06:00 PT (overnight to minimize traffic).
- Vendor IPs: 34.198.65.12, 34.198.65.13 (SyncBridge ephemeral pool).
- DocuSign is fine for runbook sign-off; procurement will need the addendum PDF to begin countersign.
- For on-call: we can accept a dedicated escalation pager number + a primary ops contact (email + phone). If you can provide that in the runbook, we can note it in our audit evidence.

Attaching: BAA_amendment_request.pdf (procurement).

Matt

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Matt Kline <matt.kline@alphamed.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-10T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: KMS access window for vendor migration — upcoming audit

Matt — thanks, all set on our side. Finalizing plan below and next actions: 

Planned schedule & controls:
- Delegation window: 2025-11-18 02:00–06:00 PT (4 hours).
- Issuance TTL: 4 hours; EPHEM will only mint tokens for allowed job IDs and the two vendor IPs you provided.
- Monitoring: we'll export a KMS issuance slice + SIEM summary within 2 business hours of window close.
- Reconciliation: Ben will run the reconciliation checklist and share a CSV of issued token IDs mapped to job runs.
- On-call: Redwood will provide a pager escalation line + primary ops contact. For this event: Pager: +1-415-555-0198 (monitor team); Ops contact: ben_carter@redwood.ai / +1-650-555-0124.

Action items:
- David: upload the runbook to the shared Drive and kick DocuSign for signatures (today).
- Laura: confirm CIDR/mTLS enforcement in the infra allowlist (by COB tomorrow).
- Ben: prepare the reconciliation template and confirm you'll own the post-runship report (ready by 11/19).
- Matt/Procurement: review BAA amendment; if redlines are needed, route to priyom_das@redwood.ai.

Attachments sent to AlphaMed: runbook_kms_delegation_v1.pdf, access_matrix_inference_v2.xlsx. DocuSign request will follow.

Thanks everyone — I'll mark this thread as the canonical audit runbook thread.

-David
David Kim
Security Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
